description: SEPARATE is a desktop and Python tool for dividing tipping-bucket rain-gauge records into storm events. It applies a selected minimum inter-event time rule, calculates storm duration, depth and intensity, and writes tables and plots with event metadata. Users provide the gauge series and threshold settings; geographic coverage and time span follow the station records, not a built-in dataset. The public repository and source documentation are MIT licensed, with installers described for Windows and macOS. Event summaries can help choose rainfall forcing and compare runoff responses in stormwater or flood simulations. A caveat is that the partitioning rule can split or combine storms differently, while gauge siting and missing tips affect intensity estimates. The installers were not downloaded, and the tool was not run on gauge data. Generic catalogue text matches for the word “separate” do not identify this named software. No related software record was found in the catalogue or first review.
